subject: Clarifying geo-binding & failback for trial deployment
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@celerityhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@celerityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: geo-binding & failback items from today's call

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a few specific clarifying questions so we can scope the trial routing and failback behavior properly.

Key items we captured:
- Primary requirement: PII and PHI storage must remain in the US for the pilot.
- Acceptable failover behavior: warm standby in another US region (not cross-border), but encrypted backups to a secondary region are acceptable if data is encrypted with a customer-managed key (KMS/HSM).
- Logs: audit logs must have identifiable event types but should be scrubbed of direct PII by default; raw request bodies retained only for 7 days unless explicitly permitted for debugging.

Clarifying questions:
1) When you say "US only for storage," do you mean both encrypted snapshots + backups must remain in US, or are geo-encrypted cross-region backups acceptable (with KMS key material anchored in the US)?
2) Expected RPO for the warm standby — is 15 minutes acceptable or do you need stricter guarantees?
3) For logging, do you need request payloads (redacted) stored longer than 7 days for audit purposes, and who should have access (security ops, product, or a named list)?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a short one-pager that maps our pinning options to the trial plan and the recommended failback path. (attached)
- If the answers above are aligned, we can schedule a 30-min technical canary next week to validate routing and key handling.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-residency-one-pager.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Ben and Marissa on legal/BAA threads if we move forward.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@celerityhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@celerityhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: geo-binding & failback items from today's call

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Clarifications below: 

1) Backups: Our security policy prefers backups remain physically within US boundaries. We can consider cross-region encrypted copies for disaster recovery only if:
   - The KMS key is customer-managed and stored in our US KMS/HSM (we do not want key material to leave the US), and
   - The backup copies in other regions are immutable and accessed only via pre-approved DR processes.

2) RPO: 15 minutes is acceptable for the pilot. Production target is 5–10 minutes, but we understand that canary/trial can be slightly laxer.

3) Logs: We want structured audit logs retained for 90 days for compliance (event metadata only); raw request payloads (containing PII/PHI) should be retained for 7 days and accessible to Security Ops and one named engineer for debugging (Priya in our case).

We need to confirm HIPAA coverage/BAA before any PHI test data is pushed. Priya — can your security/legal team confirm whether a BAA is required at pilot stage?

Also attaching our internal SOC/controls snapshot for reference.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Turner
Sr. Security Lead, Celerity Health
[Attachment: celerity-soc-controls-2028.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@celerityhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@celerityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 13:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: geo-binding & failback items from today's call

Alex — perfect, that's very helpful. Summary of our alignment and what we will include in the trial config: 

- Storage: For the pilot we will pin tenant data to a US-only region for primary storage. Cross-region encrypted immutable snapshot copies can be created to a secondary US region only, with customer-managed KMS. We cannot move key material outside the US.
- Failover: Warm standby with an RPO target of 15 minutes for the trial. We will test switchover and failback flows during the canary.
- Logs: We will provide structured audit logs retained for 90 days. Raw request payloads (containing PII/PHI) will be kept for 7 days and restricted to the security ops group + Priya by default.

Action items I will take this afternoon: 
- Send a trial routing matrix and recommended configuration (attached). [Attachment: trial-routing-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]
- Kick off a pre-trial checklist with our Compliance/Legal contact to scope BAA & HIPAA requirements — attaching a template SOW for pilot work. [Attachment: sow-trial-template.docx (DOCX, 9KB)]

Can you confirm Priya as the named engineer for payload access and confirm whether your security team is OK with our proposed immutable snapshot flow? If yes, I’ll propose two 30-minute windows next week for a canary test (Tue 03/14 10:00 or Wed 03/15 15:00 PST).

Thanks —
Diego

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@celerityhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@celerityhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: geo-binding & failback items from today's call

Diego — quick internal note and next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Good to proceed with the trial configuration as outlined. Please add Legal (legal@redwood.ai) to the thread for the BAA discussion. We should also prepare a short procurement checklist (licenses, trial SLA, data handling appendix) to send to Celerity with the SOW.
2) I’ll draft a one-paragraph executive summary for procurement that calls out: US-only primary storage, customer-managed KMS, 15-minute trial RPO, 90-day structured log retention / 7-day payload retention. Diego — can you attach that summary to the HubSpot deal record (HS-328192) once done?

If Celerity confirms Priya for access and legal confirms BAA light-touch for pilot, we greenlight the canary.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
